hook: Someone compiled a GPU into a language model's weights. It runs real CUDA.

beats.label: Qwen3.5-2B · 69 layers
beats.say: The project {qgpu|Q G P U} adds 45 layers in front of {Qwen3.5|Kwen three point five}'s own 24. No weight in them is learned. A compiler computes every one.
beats.src: README intro: 45 transformer layers in front of Qwen's own 24; none learned

scene.note: Redrawn from the project's demo · circuit layers are compiled, not trained

beats.label: A tiny SIMT GPU
beats.say: Together they form a small GPU: four lanes, a four-stage pipeline, and 126 words of memory. It handles loops, branches and warp shuffles.

scene.features: Integer arithmetic · branches · loops · shared memory · atomicAdd · __syncthreads · warp shuffles

beats.label: Gated DeltaNet recurrent state
beats.say: Registers and memory live in the recurrent state of Qwen's own Gated DeltaNet layers. Each row is one memory cell.
beats.src: README, Gated DeltaNet as GPU state

scene.note: One-hot key writes exactly one row; a one-hot query reads it back

beats.label: The model writes the launch
beats.say: The host compiles CUDA to P T X and loads it as tokens. Then the model writes the launch itself, one token for every step and value.
beats.src: README, A launch; What runs where

scene.note: Grey: written by the host · blue: generated by the model · token names from the README, sequence illustrative

beats.label: A dot product on 4 lanes
beats.say: For a dot product, each lane multiplies one pair. A warp shuffle adds them up. Every value is a token the model generated.
beats.src: README: dot product demo, warp shuffles; values here are an illustration

beats.label: Matched a real NVIDIA T4
beats.say: In the author's runs, every launch was exact. Its reference matched a real NVIDIA T4 on 49 of 49 kernels. And Qwen's normal text barely changes.

items: Every launch exact, checked token by token
Reference = real Tesla T4 on 49 of 49 kernels
Text: next-token KL about 0.0007 from Qwen

beats.label: A proof of concept
beats.say: But it is a demonstration, not a fast GPU: about 10 to 15 tokens a second. And writing its own CUDA, the 2 billion parameter model got 4 of 5 right.

items: About 10–15 tokens per second on Apple silicon
Tens to hundreds of tokens per launch
Own CUDA: 4 of 5 correct on first try
The author's results, not independently verified

outro: Source: {qgpu|Q G P U} on GitHub, built on the {Qwenputer|Kwenputer} compiler.
